Lets discuss details here @Chris Henson

abbrev arityInType (c : Type) (n : Nat) : Type :=
  match n with
  | 0 => c
  | Nat.succ n' => c → arityInType c n'

abbrev arityOutType (α : Type) : Nat → Type
    | 0 => Unit
    | n + 1 => α × arityOutType α n

class Signature (α : Type) where
  var : Nat → α
  NonVarConstructors : Type
  arity : NonVarConstructors → Nat
  construct : (c : NonVarConstructors) → arityInType α (arity c)
  destruct : α → Nat ⊕ (Σ c : NonVarConstructors, arityOutType α (arity c))
  size : α → Nat
Had something like this in mind.
For example, we have stlc types. for a Hindley milner style typechecker we need to unify types with existential variables
then we have some other calculus with some other signatures that need unification
I propose a general unification algorithm that requires an instance like this + laws consistent with some sort of Lawful HasSubst.

then we can prove stuff about that algorithm in general.

Then one only needs to implement this instance for every Type of terms that we need to unify and then we get all the unification theory, like it actually gives you an MGU for free.

Thanks for giving an mwe of these definitions. So this is an alternate definition of signatures? I'd really hoped we could use what exists in Mathlib already, which is the standard definition used in model theory and even your reference. Well, it kind of encodes the same concept, but It can be strapped on existing types

suppose we want to unify types of stlc. Then we would have to translate them into this mathlib type, then unify, and then translate back
with my definition we can just unify them directly
But I guess this comes down to personal preference

@Chris Henson https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/583 here is the pull request. but lets discuss the Typeclass interface before approving it, there are some things worth noting:

as of now, the HasParallelSubst typeclass enforces a var constructor, this means that it essentially only works for terms that allow terms that only consist of a single variable. For example, Lambda Calculus and FOL terms would work, as they admit just variables. but suppose we have the set Var x Var, this would not admit an instance. But it allows for a simple way of stating the lawful variant.

I guess I could restate it such that the typeclass supports sets like Var x Var as well if that is desireable, but then It would probably get more complicated. Also one would loose the monad instances.

@Fabrizio Montesi I would also be interested in your opinion on this pull request for this HasParallelSubst typeclass as it is quite fundamental. I want to make it such that most other parts of the library can interface with it nicely.
